title: Composing Diffusion Priors with Explicit Physical Context via Generative Gibbs Sampling
topic: Probabilistic Methods->Monte Carlo and Sampling Methods
claim: Composing a symmetric prior with physical context recovers an induced asymmetry, and replica exchange improves mixing and accuracy across diffusion times.
layout: 4 panels in one row: energy heatmap, density, two line plots
description: A single row of four plots on a white background. Panel (a) is a 2D heatmap of an asymmetric double-well energy landscape over x_sys and x_env. The colorbar runs from purple (low energy) to yellow (high energy), and two basins appear as dark blobs with the right one deeper. Panel (b) plots the marginal density of x_sys. It shows a bimodal reference curve (dashed pink), a symmetric direct-diffusion curve (dotted green), and the GG-PA (blue) and GG-PA-RE (magenta) curves, which closely track the reference. Panel (c) plots Jensen-Shannon divergence against diffusion time. Blue and magenta lines with markers rise with t, and the blue line rebounds at small t. Panel (d) plots integrated autocorrelation time on a log scale, with error bars and a dashed MD line. Blue sits well above magenta. The eye lands first on the heatmap, then on the density peaks.
caption: Coupled double-well system. (a) The environment induces an asymmetric potential. (b) Marginal density of $x_{\mathrm{sys}}$. GG-PA (blue solid) and GG-PA-RE (purple solid) capture the asymmetry despite their symmetric prior (Direct Diffusion; green dotted). (c) Jensen-Shannon divergence versus $t$. Below the diffusion time bound ($t \le 0.28$), GG-PA-RE remains consistently near the minimum observed error, whereas fixed-$t$ GG-PA rebounds at $t=0.1$ due to poor mixing. (d) Integrated autocorrelation time $\tau_{\mathrm{int}}$. Replica exchange significantly accelerates mixing.
abstract: Pretrained diffusion models provide powerful learned priors, but in scientific sampling the target distribution often depends on physical context that a single generative model can neither fully represent nor learn from scarce joint-system data. We introduce Generative Gibbs for Physics-Aware Sampling (GG-PA), a training-free framework that composes learned partial priors with explicit physical context through Gibbs sampling. We prove that this sampler is asymptotically exact as the diffusion time vanishes and remains exact at finite diffusion time for quadratic interactions. As a special case, the finite-time result corrects a finite-noise bias in plug-and-play split Gibbs samplers for linear inverse problems at no additional cost. We further introduce replica exchange over diffusion time to accelerate mixing. In experiments, a one-dimensional double-well prior recovers a context-induced distribution shift when coupled to an environment, and copies of such a prior composed on a lattice reproduce the emergent collective behavior of the $Ï^4$ model. In atomistic peptide systems, GG-PA captures a context-induced distribution shift and the spontaneous formation of hydrogen-bonded dimers from two copies of a prior trained only on the monomer.
